capabilities: Annotate Chinese notes with per-word pinyin, definitions and colors based on known/partial/unknown status
Track vocabulary exposure, HSK coverage and progress over time
Review due words with flashcard-style SRS or AI-generated stories
Explain, proofread, simplify and add mnemonics for text using an AI provider
Switch between Simplified and Traditional script and Taiwan pronunciation
extras: The bundled seed dictionary is tiny; real use expects a user-supplied CC-CEDICT file downloaded from mdbg.net. AI features (stories, explain, mnemonics, proofread) stay off until a provider is configured and send only the targeted text. No telemetry; states permissions and network endpoints in detail; docs, FAQ and install guides live in separate docs/ files.
motivation: The author found comprehensible input (as in DuChinese) made learning Chinese enjoyable, but flashcards broke the flow once rare words stopped appearing often enough in reading.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to turn Chinese notes into level-appropriate reading with per-word support, vocabulary tracking, or story-based spaced repetition.

relations.evidence: Tools such as DuChinese have shown how powerful this approach can be.
The bundled seed dictionary is tiny; real use needs CC-CEDICT (see Data below).
Ollama tips: model choice and getting good output
Formatting & highlighting — tap-to-format mode, colored highlights, Highlightr support

summary: Chinese reading environment that annotates notes with dictionary-aware pinyin, definitions and knowledge-status colors, plus vocabulary tracking, SRS and AI story generation.
